items.reason: Needs network: pinning means asking GitHub what each tag points at right now, and an invented SHA breaks a workflow rather than pinning it; the repository already ships the exact one-command path (`npm run actions:pin` resolves every tag to its digest, rewrites the seven workflows, and writes STRICT = true plus RATCHET.pinned = <count> back into scripts/actions-pin.mjs so both halves land in one diff), so there is nothing left to build offline — only a networked run to make.

Needs a typecheck run: putting `typecheck:strict` into check:ci means first knowing whether the tree passes it, and this session has no shell — promoting it blind is what ADR-0007 and tsconfig.strict.json's own header both forbid. What I could close offline I did: `typecheck:strict` appeared NOWHERE outside package.json and its own file (not AGENTS.md, not docs/task-index.md), so an agent following the documented loop could not meet it at all; it is now in AGENTS.md § Commands and routed from the task index, and test-unit/typecheck-strict.test.mjs (blocking, inside test:unit → check:ci → pre-push) fails when the script and config diverge, when the strict project stops measuring any flag the base project does not, when the config stops saying why it is not a gate, or when it IS added to check:ci while still claiming 'NOT A GATE'.

Needs a run to mint the numbers: every candidate budget (a route's p95, the dashboard's LCP, the cost of the gate chain) has to record today's measurement before it can fail on a regression, and a ceiling I invented would be decoration. Two concrete findings for whoever picks this up: the accept-with-a-reason artefact already exists (.github/gate-timings.json, written by `npm run check:ci:timed` then `npm run gates:timings -- --accept --reason "…"`) but has NEVER been recorded, so `gates:timings --check` returns 0 with 'No gate timings recorded yet'; and even once recorded, orderingProblems() in scripts/gate-timings.mjs only judges cheapest-first ORDER — no stage has a duration ceiling, so a gate that doubles in cost stays green.

A repo-local flag layer (deterministic bucketing on the tenant key, a committed ledger of what is behind a flag and when it came off, a unit test holding the ledger true) is buildable with no dependency and is the right shape under ADR-0008 — but it only counts as staged exposure if it is WIRED, and every seam the item names (the LLM chokepoint, billing/metering, the Sklik write guard) is a CODEOWNERS law file that AGENTS.md § Red puts off-limits to an unattended run; wiring it anywhere else makes it a stub. With no shell I also cannot typecheck, build or test a new src/lib module, and landing unverified code into a repository whose test:unit baseline is already red would be indistinguishable from the failure that is there. The decision left is the operator's: name the first cohorted seam and whether Vercel-side canarying or an in-app percentage flag is the mechanism.

Needs git and a hook path outside this repository: the rules already exist (scripts/commit-attribution.mjs defines the trailer, `npm run commit:check --range` prints coverage, `npm run review:agent` lists unattributed commits) and the reason they are not honoured is mechanical — the Ascent lane commits in a linked worktree with no `.husky/_`, so git runs no hook whatever core.hooksPath says, and `.husky/` is a permission-gated path for these sessions. Making it blocking additionally needs today's coverage over history, which needs git; a richer trailer (agent, model, harness version) is worth writing only once something actually writes it.

lessons: Eight consecutive lanes on this repository have been told to repair `npm run test:unit` FIRST, and not one of them could run it: the lane sandbox refuses `npm` and `node` outright (only read-only shell verbs like ls/cat/grep are allowed) and the priority block says 'read the output below' while including no output. The repair is not converging because nobody has ever seen the failure — the fix is on the harness side (attach the failing output, or grant the one command), not in the tree.

This worktree's node_modules is a SYMLINK to the main checkout (C:/Users/kazda/kiro/systedo-case/node_modules), which the lane sandbox actively blocks reading. If the lane runs the suite under the same sandbox, every bare-specifier import resolves outside the permitted directory — an environment-level failure no source change can fix, and one that would look identical on every lane. Worth ruling out before another agent-hours are spent bisecting 472 test files.

When an item's honest close needs a measurement (a tsc run, a p95, a digest), say so and close the DISCOVERABILITY half instead: this repository's own idiom is an index plus a unit test that goes red when the artefact and the routing drift (docs-task-index.test.mjs, agent-index.test.mjs), and it transfers to 'why is this command not a gate?' without inventing a baseline.

Every seam worth putting behind a staged rollout in this repository is a CODEOWNERS law file that AGENTS.md § Red forbids an unattended run from touching. Flag infrastructure is therefore not an agent-closable item here however small the code is — the wiring decision has to come from the operator first, or the agent ships a library nothing calls.
